cards.front: Recall a key point about Evaluating Performance and Design
cards.back: Evaluation = analysis + judgement. You must say HOW effective something was AND WHY.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Evaluating Performance and Design
cards.back: Criteria for evaluation: did the choice serve the production's intention? Did it communicate meaning clearly? Did it engage the audience?

cards.front: Recall a key point about Evaluating Performance and Design
cards.back: Support every judgement with SPECIFIC evidence from the production — never make unsupported claims.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Evaluating Performance and Design
cards.back: Performance evaluation: vocal skills, physical skills, characterisation, interaction. Design evaluation: set, costume, lighting, sound, props.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Evaluating Performance and Design
cards.back: Link choices to the production's OVERALL INTENTION — a choice is effective if it serves the vision, not just if it was impressive.

cards.front: What should you know about drama exam tips?
cards.back: For evaluation questions, use the structure: What I saw (specific moment) → How it was done (technique) → What it meant (analysis) → How effective it was (judgement) → Why it was effective/ineffective (reasoning linked to intention). This ensures both analysis and evaluation are present.
Was it truthful and engaging? (e.g. Specific performance moments)
Did the concept serve the text? (e.g. Overall production choices)
Did it create appropriate world? (e.g. Visual documentation)
Did it communicate character? (e.g. Production photos)
Did it shape mood and focus? (e.g. Lighting states described)
Did it create atmosphere? (e.g. Sound cues described)

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: Evaluating a production means saying whether it was good or bad and whether you enjoyed it. Correct: Evaluation is about EFFECTIVENESS, not personal taste. A choice is effective if it serves the production's intention, communicates meaning clearly and impacts the audience as intended. Evaluate the effectiveness of the performance and design choices in a production you have seen. Support your evaluation with specific examples.

Live theatre evaluation tests AO2 (analyse and evaluate — 20% of the qualification). In Section B of the written exam, you must write about a production you have seen. Marks are awarded for: precise analysis of specific moments, supported judgements about effectiveness, use of theatrical terminology, and understanding of how choices serve the production's intention.
